chapter: Young players, schools and studio work
title: Dress and cleanliness for work
summary: Maxwell says hygiene and neatness matter to getting hired.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Quite true. I just wanted some semblance of what's required because this is what we're trying to get into young people.

Yeah, I think, too, you know, this business of wearing a hat and tank shirt and dirty sneakers and that kind of stuff; I think dress has -- I was going to say a small importance, but actually it's got a big importance. I don't mean you have to show up in a jacket and tie, but you do have to show up fairly neat and you should take a bath once in a while. And I'm not talking about black, I'm talking mostly white musicians I know. But I guess black musicians do this, too. They show up, they don't bathe all weak, they wear these stinking tank shirts and they're barefoot or something. And they smell. And, you know, they make an uneasy feeling and

they're not going to be hired again if they do these things. I don't care how much they want to, quote, do their thing or express themselves. When you're working for a guy, you may not like his rules but those are the rules and he's hiring you and you'd better follow them if you want to work.
